Evidence & scope

Substantive bounded primary methods/results/limitations source review is documented at 2305.06161v2. Human-inspected corpus/PII data methods and licensing/opt-out caveats establish curation scope; title andv2header match. License-detector and PII limitations remain, no corpus-rights audit inferred. Original author/source-verifier/adversarial receipts bind every exact approved fact; unread pages, unreplicated experiments and source conflicts remain recorded in the pinned dossier. This admission is for one logical paper work only.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The authors warn that license detection can misclassify repositories, repository-level opt-out can miss copied code, and PII detection has false positives/negatives; PII annotations are gated to approved individuals and published model evaluations are English-only.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

StarCoder curation combined extension-level community inspection and source-code filters with a PII detector: human-labeled examples trained StarEncoder token classification for names, emails, keys, passwords, IP addresses and usernames; IDs were excluded because of poor annotation quality.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Toloka engaged 1, 399 workers from 35 countries to label 12, 000 roughly 50-line files in 31 languages; 7, 100 files were prefiltered to enrich rare PII and 5, 100 were random. Annotators found 22, 950 entities, and authors manually inspected 300 files for QC.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

The fine-tuned PII baseline reports F1 above 90% for names, emails andIP addresses, 73.39% for passwords, 56.66% for keys and 59.39% for usernames; the split was 7, 878 training and 4, 000 test examples, supplemented in training by 400 earlier annotated files.
